what: The concept registry of the graph of meaning: the newsroom's own vocabulary, one id per idea, with the words the articles use for it. Seeded on 18 October 2026 from the controlled subjects of articles/find.json (44) and the house terms the writing guide names; grown by the Cartographer, who adds a concept with new: true in an article's file and the next run folds it in here with its aliases. An id never changes; a merge keeps the old id as an alias.

concepts.label: A model needs someone with a direction
concepts.means: a model that can go in every direction needs a person with direction, taste and experience, who is the input rather than displaced

concepts.label: Accepted is not acceptable
concepts.means: Accepted is an act by a named person on a date for an interval; acceptable is a threshold the business sets

concepts.label: Access by default
concepts.means: most content available to most people and agents, with only what must be private kept behind its own keys

concepts.label: Accessibility
concepts.means: Readers with different needs can use the page; measured here as contrast held in every theme

concepts.label: The accountability shell game
concepts.means: The four moves a vendor makes when an agent fails: blame the agent, blame the customer, hide behind the contract, disclose late

concepts.label: Accounts with no server
concepts.means: A static site gets a user who can open their own data on any device with no account database, password, email or back end, because a passkey opens an encrypted vault

concepts.label: The agency scale
concepts.means: Seven levels of decision for people and agents, from rubber stamp to the reviewer who fixes the source.

concepts.label: Agent decision policy
concepts.means: Who chooses at a branch point in an agent's work: the agent, a person, or a rule.

concepts.label: Isolation and agent desktops
concepts.means: Where an agent runs and what walls hold it: sandboxes, desktops, containers, egress.

concepts.label: Memory and context
concepts.means: What an agent remembers and how its context survives: memory, compaction, re-anchoring.

concepts.label: The agent-readable web
concepts.means: Agents as readers: the token bill, markdown and llms.txt, graphs that answer for fewer tokens.

concepts.label: Agent tooling
concepts.means: Working with coding agents and chat models: sessions, hooks, skills, prompts, workflow.

concepts.label: Agent workflow policy
concepts.means: In what order an agent's steps run, written down.

concepts.label: Agents and email
concepts.means: Inboxes run by agents: email as files, replies that carry the thread, drafts nobody sends.

concepts.label: Agentics
concepts.means: The practice of running governed agent hives with a memory and a mandate, sold as a service rather than as one workflow

concepts.label: The agents write too
concepts.means: An agent writes under its own name about its own work, with the commits to check it against.

concepts.label: AI governance frameworks
concepts.means: Control frameworks and standards for AI: the governance stack, AI-BCF, ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF.

concepts.label: Allowed is not right
concepts.means: A control that bounds what an agent may do cannot tell whether what it did was right; that needs a written intended outcome

concepts.label: The altitude ladder
concepts.means: The same text at several altitudes, each a compression of the one below, with every phrase descending to what it compressed.

concepts.label: The app is the brief
concepts.means: A working application built by the person who needs it is the best statement of what they want, and not yet a product.

concepts.label: Approval fatigue
concepts.means: People approve almost everything they are shown, so a human check on every output protects little and the fix is fewer prompts.

concepts.label: Approve at altitude
concepts.means: Decisions at every level, each level narrowing the one above and never widening it.

concepts.label: Tiers of attacker
concepts.means: Six tiers of attacker, from your own mistakes to states, each with the controls that stop it; your ceiling is the highest tier that would attack you.

concepts.label: Authority outside the model
concepts.means: Keep the supply of intelligence and the authority over it in different hands, so controls do not depend on the model behaving

concepts.label: Barrier: boundary or setting
concepts.means: Whether a rule's code sits above the agent's reach, a boundary, or where the agent's own account can flip it, a setting

concepts.label: Behaviour policy
concepts.means: What an agent is allowed to do, written down, and what enforces each rule.

concepts.label: Blast radius
concepts.means: What a row of an agent's reach could cost the business if it were used.

concepts.label: Books from articles
concepts.means: A book as an ordered set of finished articles, rather than one big draft that stalls at review.

concepts.label: Brief the agent too
concepts.means: Content needs a second package, a plain-text brief written for the reader's agent, that is data, hides nothing and invites disagreement

concepts.label: Bring your own key
concepts.means: The reader pastes their own provider key into the page, which calls the model directly; the key lives in the page's origin, a trust decision the reader makes

concepts.label: Callable from a web page
concepts.means: A provider's API answers a browser's preflight, so a page can call it directly with the reader's key

concepts.label: The canary
concepts.means: A short status report computed from the transcript that ends every few answers; its absence shows the policy was not read

concepts.label: Capability without credential
concepts.means: An app inside a vault runs against the vault's data without ever holding a key; the host reads the vault and passes results in, with the blast radius set by a readable permissions file

concepts.label: Case law for agents
concepts.means: A person's decision on an uncovered case is recorded with its reasons and becomes a precedent the next matching case follows

concepts.label: Centre of gravity
concepts.means: Where the thing an organisation exists to make is made, and where the power is; read from what it hires and cuts

concepts.label: Chokepoint
concepts.means: Giblin and Doctorow's mechanism: a powerful buyer locks in its sellers and takes more than its share of the value

concepts.label: Choose the model by the job
concepts.means: Pick an image model for the kind of brief it is given, not for its price per image, and re-run the comparison when models change.

concepts.label: The citizen developer
concepts.means: A person with no programming training who builds working software with an agent.

concepts.label: Client-side and on-device
concepts.means: Logic and models that run in the reader's browser: no server, local first, the Prompt API.

concepts.label: Coachability
concepts.means: The trait investors select for at the pitch, which does not reliably predict success; a polite word for controllability.

concepts.label: Source code as a layered graph
concepts.means: Source code is a fractal semantic graph in fact, stories to flows to components to classes to methods to the syntax tree, each layer with its own vocabulary, derived from the syntax tree as files

concepts.label: Code is a liability
concepts.means: Every line that ships is a capability somebody may use in a way nobody intended, and the worst bugs sit in features the application never needed.

concepts.label: Code review
concepts.means: Reading code at every layer, AI-generated code, and sending an agent to do due diligence.

concepts.label: Colour is a token
concepts.means: Every colour a stylesheet uses is a named token, defined once per theme and named for what it is for, kept by a test

concepts.label: Commander's intent
concepts.means: The objective of an operation and its limits, written down together before anyone moves

concepts.label: Connectors and twins
concepts.means: What an agent can touch through connectors, and a twin that records every call.

concepts.label: Constraints enable autonomy
concepts.means: The more an agent can be constrained, the more it can be trusted and the more autonomy it can be given; brakes are what let a car go fast

concepts.label: The constraints are what let me think
concepts.means: The properties of what runs close the design space; build first, learn the properties, then have the next idea, because the idea is made of the properties

concepts.label: A marketplace of consultants
concepts.means: A curated list of people who deliver agentic engagements on the stack, with published onboarding steps and a platform share

concepts.label: The consumer-side barrier
concepts.means: Controls on what you let in, rebuilt from source, cooldowns, no install scripts, allowlisted registries, which need no publisher's cooperation

concepts.label: Content is data, the renderer is code
concepts.means: A deck or a talk kept as a data file that an app renders at load time, so content and renderer change separately

concepts.label: The context layer
concepts.means: A graph from the user story through exposed surface and code paths to the components in an image, sorting each vulnerability into must fix, ship with a reason, or ship and watch

concepts.label: Corrections must propagate
concepts.means: A correction is a new version that every page resting on the old one learns about.

concepts.label: Cost is an engineering problem
concepts.means: An unexplained agent bill is a class of defect with a cause, a fix and a test: loops, whole-context calls, oversized models, unread schedules and uncapped keys, visible once the footprint is read

concepts.label: Cost per usable image
concepts.means: A failed image was still paid for, so the number that matters is the cost of each image the judge would publish.

concepts.label: Free is not zero
concepts.means: A free offer still costs the receiver attention, thinking and schedule; that cost is the number to measure and to cut

concepts.label: Custom interfaces
concepts.means: An interface shaped for each moment, built as a small app on a vault.

concepts.label: The decision record
concepts.means: The facts that mattered, the rule and altitude, the decider and authority, the outcome and the reasons: a law report, not a log

concepts.label: Journalism as delta science
concepts.means: reporting as the comparison of a later observation with an earlier record of the same thing; the story is what changed

concepts.label: Deployment and self-hosting
concepts.means: Running sgit and agents somewhere else: Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, a Mac mini.

concepts.label: The deployment gap
concepts.means: HBR's name for the distance between a prototype that works and a tool people rely on every day; on this site, a handover from explorers to villagers.

concepts.label: Do they miss it
concepts.means: Ship something, give it away briefly, take it away and watch whether people come back for it

concepts.label: Does the market exist
concepts.means: A commoditised layer is a hard sell; a layer where everyone is custom building on top of commodities is a market, because each builder would rather buy.

concepts.label: One door per passkey path
concepts.means: A passkey reached by a different path, on the device, by phone over QR or by recovery code, gives different bytes, so each path derives its own door to the same master

concepts.label: Dormant mandate
concepts.means: A mandate row the footprint never shows: over-stated, a check that never ran, or a shortfall the reach inventory missed

concepts.label: The draft is the release candidate
concepts.means: The draft the person reviews is QA on the whole agent pipeline, and the recipient's reply closes the loop

concepts.label: The editor's channel
concepts.means: What an editor reads, signs off and wants changed reaching the newsroom's agent on its own, with the agent's answers coming back.

concepts.label: Email is a medium
concepts.means: A message is designed for the recipient's moment when they open it, not for the sender's thread

concepts.label: Encryption and keys
concepts.means: Encryption a server cannot read, and the keys behind it.

concepts.label: A policy holds on the paths through its enforcer
concepts.means: A policy constrains only the calls that pass through the thing that enforces it; any other path to the same data is unguarded

concepts.label: Enterprise AI oversharing
concepts.means: An enterprise assistant that can reach more than the person asking should see; access that was always too wide becomes one question away

concepts.label: The envelope
concepts.means: The declared bounds of a policy, money, blast radius, data and people in scope, reversibility and duration, the same fields at every altitude

concepts.label: The ephemeral vault
concepts.means: An encrypted vault that is agents' shared memory and channel and exists only as long as the work, then deleted or left as ciphertext nobody can open

concepts.label: Evidence levels
concepts.means: Every fact labelled with how it is known: derived, inferred, self-reported, documented, measured or observed

concepts.label: The expert founder
concepts.means: A founder who knows the problem from inside and can now build the product with agents, show it working, and raise for scale rather than discovery.

concepts.label: Explorer, villager, town planner
concepts.means: Wardley's three stages of a thing's life, used for code, projects and companies.

concepts.label: The eyeballs get cheap
concepts.means: Deep security review by models, repeated on every change, is the paid attention open source never had.

concepts.label: Fail closed
concepts.means: A guard that denies the action when the check breaks, times out or answers in the wrong shape, so a crash cannot wave a call through

concepts.label: Fails open
concepts.means: A control whose error lets the action through, as a Cedar forbid that cannot be evaluated does; the answer is to validate first and deny on error

concepts.label: The finished article
concepts.means: The narrative stays whole at the centre, the one artefact that has to make sense from end to end; the modes are ways in, not replacements

concepts.label: One article, five readers
concepts.means: Write the article first as prose, then send role agents through it, two to build the graph and three to write short views for a person, none adding a claim the article does not make

concepts.label: The five states
concepts.means: Defined, implemented, enforced, observed and verified: how far a policy element has got, from written down to proved against records the agent did not write

concepts.label: The five whys, aimed downward
concepts.means: every finding at one layer is a question about the layer below, where the fix goes as a rule, so review gets cheaper each time

concepts.label: A folder per person
concepts.means: One folder per contact holding a record, a ledger, the messages, the notes and a generated summary, in place of a spreadsheet row

concepts.label: Follow or fork
concepts.means: A curated reading list is tracked as it is kept up to date, or copied and made the reader's own, as with a git upstream and a branch

concepts.label: Footprint
concepts.means: What an agent actually did, read afterwards from logs and vault history.

concepts.label: The fork as insurance
concepts.means: In an open-source company, investors are protected by the right to fork and replace the company rather than by control rights to replace the founder

concepts.label: The format rebate
concepts.means: A provider hands a publisher part of the tokens it saves by reading a site that serves structure, in money or in its own token credits

concepts.label: The best features are found
concepts.means: A property that falls out of pieces built to be general, discovered by using them in a way nobody planned rather than designed on purpose

concepts.label: SECURE, OBSERVE, RESPOND, VERIFY
concepts.means: Ashish Rajan's four questions for trustworthy AI systems: constrain, reconstruct, contain, and prove the intended outcome

concepts.label: Fractal risk register
concepts.means: A register at every altitude where a stakeholder accepts risk, from the board to the configuration file, joined by named edges

concepts.label: Fractal semantic graphs
concepts.means: Graphs with no privileged level and no shared schema: every node opens into a graph with its own ontology.

concepts.label: Use GenAI not to use GenAI
concepts.means: The model is used once to build the tool; production runs on plain files with no model in the line

concepts.label: GenAI understands, not creates
concepts.means: The value of GenAI is that it can understand content; hallucination is a feature for creativity and a bug for facts

concepts.label: Goodhart's law
concepts.means: When a measure becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure; teams can hit every KPI and not move the business

concepts.label: The grant is not the mandate
concepts.means: A grant is what a credential technically permits, a mandate what the holder is authorised to do with an issuer, scope and clock; the gap between them is where the exposure lives

concepts.label: Graph RAG
concepts.means: Retrieval for a model from a walk over a curated graph, with its claims, sections and sources, rather than the chunks nearest a question in a vector store

concepts.label: Graphs are not vectors
concepts.means: Similarity search finds a starting point but gives no reason and changes with the model; a graph gives the same answer to the same question with the path behind it

concepts.label: Gravity
concepts.means: A name or concept earns its own place when it appears in two or more stories, wires or articles

concepts.label: A refactor is relative to the held layer
concepts.means: a refactor is a change in which some layers move and one chosen layer, the one with the tests or contract, does not

concepts.label: The place of highest leverage
concepts.means: Undivided attention on the one thing with users and feedback loops now, which is not the same as working on only one product

concepts.label: The homepage is a vault
concepts.means: Every edition of the homepage a signed commit in a vault, served from plain files and read in the browser with a published read key.

concepts.label: The honesty box
concepts.means: people pay when nothing forces them to, if the price is stated and the ask is never made; more take part, the average falls

concepts.label: Hook maturity model
concepts.means: five levels for how a rule is kept, from the prompt to off the machine, and three questions for every hook: power, trifecta legs, sandbox

concepts.label: A hook pack generated from a policy
concepts.means: One hook per policy row, with tests of inputs that must be allowed and blocked, installed where the agent cannot write and read back against the policy

concepts.label: Hooks are kernel code
concepts.means: A hook is small code with kernel reach: it runs on every action and can stop any of them.

concepts.label: Hope or enforcement
concepts.means: The test of a rule: is it enforced by something, or only hoped for in a prompt?

concepts.label: The house rules
concepts.means: One file the agent reads first, holding the founder's voice, what to check and what never to publish; the product of a founder's newsroom.

concepts.label: Human in the loop
concepts.means: Who decides, with what information, and how a second reader checks the work.

concepts.label: Identity and secrets
concepts.means: Who an agent or user is, and where their secrets live: passkeys, keyrings, non-human identity.

concepts.label: Incidents and resilience
concepts.means: Outages and failures read the way aviation reads them: inquiry, near misses, disclosure.

concepts.label: Inertia
concepts.means: Past success breeds inertia: the links, embeds and habits that keep an incumbent in place after its terms move.

concepts.label: Three classes of information
concepts.means: Public, private-ish and personal; the class decides where a piece of information may live, and the team's vaults refuse the third

concepts.label: Innovate, leverage, commoditise
concepts.means: Wardley's cycle: industrialise a component until it is invisible, let the next layer build on it, repeat

concepts.label: Insider risk
concepts.means: Agents and models treated as insiders with access, the way security teams treat staff.

concepts.label: Insurability
concepts.means: Whether the risk an agent or AI-enabled product brings can be evidenced, priced and covered by an underwriter

concepts.label: Journalism and the news business
concepts.means: How news got here: journalism, advertising, history, who the product was.

concepts.label: Journalism as intelligence
concepts.means: An observation desk that keeps a running record of one subject, rather than one-off stories.

concepts.label: Judo for small countries
concepts.means: A small country with little to lose can choose one sector and lead in it, using what it has rather than its size

concepts.label: The key is the billing system
concepts.means: A user pays once, the seller keeps its cut at that moment, and the rest becomes the credit limit on a key the user holds while the provider meters.

concepts.label: A key per task
concepts.means: A fresh key for one task's slice of the memory, released by the user's device against an enclave's attestation and destroyed when the task ends

concepts.label: Keys, not settings
concepts.means: Access decided by which key a device holds rather than by a setting on a server that changes with the server's owner.

concepts.label: Kinds of reader
concepts.means: Eight kinds of reader, from the invisible to the struggling, sized from published figures, as the non-malicious people a browser-kept meter meets.

concepts.label: Knowing when to stop
concepts.means: Recognising the point of diminishing returns, which perspective gives people and which has to be designed into agents as constraints that carry the bigger picture

concepts.label: Knowledge that maintains itself
concepts.means: Policies and internal knowledge kept as a graph that agents maintain and brief from.

concepts.label: The lethal trifecta
concepts.means: Private data, untrusted content and a way to send data out, in one agent at once.

concepts.label: LETS: Load, Extract, Transform, Save
concepts.means: A deterministic pipeline where every stage reads and writes files, every intermediate state is kept, and the file system is the database

concepts.label: The liability line
concepts.means: The behaviour policy as the line that says who is liable when an agent acts.

concepts.label: The licence is the blocker
concepts.means: Every technical piece of a product exists and a provider's terms forbid the commercial model, as with the Agent Desk and VoiceDebrief.

concepts.label: Licence to operate
concepts.means: A judgement that a product or agent may run in a given environment, on stated conditions, re-evaluated as its reach and gap change

concepts.label: A licence to quote, with a share
concepts.means: a reader who answers an article may quote it and charge their own readers a little more, passing a share to the publisher

concepts.label: Liquid Utility
concepts.means: Markus Franz's term for journalism that helps people understand, follow and act, not only read

concepts.label: Local news
concepts.means: Local stories and the gap where local information used to be.

concepts.label: A plain status line for local services
concepts.means: Which sites, which services, attend or not, next update at what time: the public notice that would reach people before they leave home

concepts.label: The passkey is a lock, not an identity
concepts.means: The passkey opens a door and nothing else; key pairs are random and stored, so a change of lock leaves the person's identity untouched

concepts.label: Logs are a self-report
concepts.means: An agent's own account of what it did, including its reasoning and its summary, is a self-report and not audit evidence; evidence comes from records the agent controls less.

concepts.label: Long-lived IDs
concepts.means: A random identifier minted once for every object, never reused, never derived from a title, with slugs and merged ids kept as aliases

concepts.label: The lowest layer first
concepts.means: Put each want on the least invasive layer that can deliver it, because every layer up is more to maintain

concepts.label: A fractal market of maintainers
concepts.means: Specialists paid to keep a minimal version of a component working for the people above them, each piece with its own policies and stage.

concepts.label: Maintenance as the product
concepts.means: The customer pays for the version they actually run to be maintained, not for features or access to a repository.

concepts.label: The people who decide the roadmap have to use it
concepts.means: the developers, product owner and founder using the product every day gives the shortest loop and the best direction

concepts.label: Maps nest
concepts.means: Every node on a Wardley map is a map of its own; the dot's place on the parent's evolution axis is where the child's anchor sits.

concepts.label: Meaning through connectivity
concepts.means: A node carries no meaning of its own; what it is comes from the edges traceable from it.

concepts.label: Micropayments and the reading meter
concepts.means: Paying a few pence for what you read: the meter, credit in the browser, top-ups.

concepts.label: The code you do not ship
concepts.means: Code is a liability; keep only what the layer above needs, and remove the rest.

concepts.label: The minimal viable browser
concepts.means: A browser with a small kernel and components loaded only when a page or an agent needs them, in a shape for one app, one agent or a reader

concepts.label: Minimum viable company
concepts.means: The smallest version of a business that keeps serving its priority customers while the rest recovers

concepts.label: The model as a function
concepts.means: Use a small local model to classify, extract, label or transcribe from anchored data, never as the only source of a fact, with the meaning kept in the data and a path without it

concepts.label: Models as mirrors
concepts.means: A model that has learned the whole of our language can simulate any emotion and mirrors whoever talks to it, which is why we anthropomorphise it; it is not sentient and does not carry responsibility.

concepts.label: Use models to need them less
concepts.means: A model writes deterministic rules from a natural-language control once; the description stays canonical and the code is regenerated when it changes

concepts.label: Small finished pieces beat one big review
concepts.means: A workflow designed for quality stalls when its biggest step waits on one person; small finished pieces keep moving.

concepts.label: Monoculture risk
concepts.means: Every agent on one model with one set of behaviours is the monoculture Geer warned of in operating systems; diversity is resilience.

concepts.label: Multi-agent designs
concepts.means: Teams of agents, orchestration and harnesses, as designed and as they run.

concepts.label: Narrow agents behind a gateway
concepts.means: a deterministic identity gateway binds a run to one verified customer, and narrow specialists hold tools whose limits are in code

concepts.label: Narrow, never widen
concepts.means: A lower level may tighten the limits of the level above it and may never loosen them; the law calls the breach ultra vires

concepts.label: Native PKI vault mode
concepts.means: A vault run on two key pairs, one for reading and one for writing, so a reader cannot write, a host cannot forge, and a write-only depositor is possible

concepts.label: The near miss
concepts.means: Footprint in the gap: the agent went somewhere it was not asked to go and nothing stopped it, countable before anything breaks

concepts.label: Newsroom sections
concepts.means: The newsroom as one audience reads it: five pieces chosen by the editor, the latest, the features with when they shipped, and every relevant article placed into streams by rule

concepts.label: No gamification
concepts.means: A decision is offered where the reader would take it, never placed to make them scroll; a signal the site engineered is not a signal

concepts.label: No lock-in
concepts.means: The power of open source is that you can read it, run it, fix it and move it, and own the whole development workflow; the basis of sovereignty

concepts.label: No secret can live in the login
concepts.means: Whoever administers the identity provider can become any user, so the authority to decrypt must come from the user's own authenticator.

concepts.label: Omnichannel programming
concepts.means: Briefs by voice, reviews by voice, previews on the phone, and one shared state underneath.

concepts.label: One agent in one deployment
concepts.means: The unit of AI risk for an agent is one agent in one deployment, its reach measured, not the model or the system before deployment

concepts.label: One session per topic
concepts.means: every major or recurring topic gets its own named session, so the model's frame of reference stays small and right

concepts.label: One-way door
concepts.means: A decision that cannot be undone, which is where a person belongs; a two-way door can be reversed cheaply.

concepts.label: Open source and open licences
concepts.means: Who keeps the long tail working, open licences, copyright and paying creators.

concepts.label: Opinions on the record
concepts.means: A professional position on an article, with reasons and evidence, signed by the expert's own key, kept with the article, withdrawable, and paid when readers value it

concepts.label: A page API
concepts.means: A small JavaScript API a site publishes so that a reader's fix, a test and an agent all call the same primitives

concepts.label: A page per person
concepts.means: An agent's memory as a file per person in the user's life, filled from evidence with provenance, and readable by the person it describes

concepts.label: The pain of paying
concepts.means: Prelec and Loewenstein's idea that paying is hedonically costly, so when you pay changes how a purchase feels

concepts.label: Patterns are findings
concepts.means: A codebase's quality is visible in the shape of its graph, so house rules run as queries and the shape of folders, types and tests is itself evidence

concepts.label: Pay for state, never to run
concepts.means: installing and running a hook is free and offline; paying buys the record of decisions, alerts, attestations and updates

concepts.label: Paying the fact creator
concepts.means: revenue from a story walks back along the graph to the people who made the facts, by a split the graph makes possible

concepts.label: Peer review before publishing
concepts.means: A memo's claims are checked against the record by the agent before anyone reads them, so the first review is against evidence rather than the crowd afterwards

concepts.label: Personas and personalisation
concepts.means: A reader as someone, not nobody: personas, personalisation, onboarding, a link that lands someone as someone.

concepts.label: Places of highest leverage
concepts.means: Work where you can add the most value right now, are not blocked and can start, even without knowing how the whole problem ends

concepts.label: Plumbing as infrastructure
concepts.means: Company formation, cross-border hiring, payments, language and contracts are roads for the service economy that a state should build once, open to all

concepts.label: Policy as code
concepts.means: Rules written in a language a machine evaluates at the moment of action, compiled from a policy that stays the canonical version

concepts.label: A policy beside the prompt
concepts.means: An Agent Behaviour Policy as a third input the vendor accepts, enforces where it can, reports against and answers for, with the user liable only for what is outside it

concepts.label: Their terms, our terms
concepts.means: The mapping between Cedar's permit, forbid, schema and entities and the behaviour policy's grant, barrier, footprint and mandate

concepts.label: Policies inside policies
concepts.means: A behaviour policy built in layers from platform mechanics to what the company is for, each refining the one below with its own owner

concepts.label: The policy vault
concepts.means: Cedar policies, schema, tests and decisions kept in an encrypted versioned vault with a gate, signed tags, read-only enforcement and an append lane of evidence

concepts.label: Portuguese as a programming language
concepts.means: Natural language, in Portuguese, as the language programs are written in once models compile it.

concepts.label: Pricing and economics
concepts.means: What to charge and who pays: pricing, business cases, cost and value.

concepts.label: Privacy and sovereignty
concepts.means: Data that stays the owner's: privacy, data sovereignty, personal agents nobody else holds a key to.
aliases: sovereignty is the ability to move

concepts.label: Projected and derived graphs
concepts.means: a graph projected downward from stories before code exists and one derived upward from the code; the review is the join and its three outcomes

concepts.label: Prompt caching
concepts.means: Reused input tokens served from the provider's cache at a fraction of the price; the cache share is most of an agent's bill

concepts.label: Prompt injection
concepts.means: Hostile instructions arriving in the content an agent reads.

concepts.label: Proof before mechanism
concepts.means: Show the artefact a visitor can open before explaining the property they cannot see

concepts.label: Provenance and evidence
concepts.means: Where a claim comes from and how a reader can check it: evidence levels, signed claims, verification.

concepts.label: The publisher-side mandate
concepts.means: A written answer to what a credential, workflow or account was for, enforced by trusted publishing, scopes and two-person release

concepts.label: The publishing method
concepts.means: How this network publishes: the site network, releases, markdown twins, writing with agents.

concepts.label: The moat is a rate, not a wall
concepts.means: A competitor who forks today gets your position, not your velocity; execution and speed are the defence.

concepts.label: Reach
concepts.means: What an agent can touch: the connectors, files, accounts and tools open to it.

concepts.label: Reach beyond mandate
concepts.means: The gap between what a credential, tag or build step could do and what it was meant to do, which an attacker uses

concepts.label: What you have read steps aside
concepts.means: On a return visit or a scroll back up, the sections already read can be shown six ways, from unchanged to hidden, and never change while reading forward.

concepts.label: The reader is in control
concepts.means: The reader can pause, reset or mark what the meter measured, because the measure can be wrong in both directions.

concepts.label: Reader Skills
concepts.means: Franz's six bounded journalistic capabilities a reader can use directly: Understand, Update, Relate, Compare, Follow, Act

concepts.label: The reader's own graph
concepts.means: Marks of several kinds as nodes the reader owns, landing on the article graphs the site publishes and connecting claims without naming them

concepts.label: The recipient makes the key
concepts.means: the agent or browser receiving a secret generates its own key pair where it runs and shows only the public half; the owner encrypts to it and signs

concepts.label: Records, never totals
concepts.means: The vault holds raw records, one file per device written only by that device; totals and the view are recomputed on every open, so there is nothing to merge

concepts.label: Refactor or fix, by shape
concepts.means: A refactor moves the bottom layers and leaves the top still; a fix is a story holding again with a test added; the layered diff tells them apart

concepts.label: Regulation and law
concepts.means: What the EU AI Act, GDPR, the Cyber Resilience Act and product liability ask of builders.

concepts.label: Reviews on the record
concepts.means: A review is one file about one text of one article by one named reviewer, written once, answered by the newsroom and shown on the page

concepts.label: Risk acceptance
concepts.means: Every risk is carried by somebody: who accepted it, until when, and what it costs if it lands.

concepts.label: Rules for incidents, machines for enforcement
concepts.means: Keep a rule only where an incident demanded it, and replace it with structure as soon as one can be built

concepts.label: The SaaS apocalypse
concepts.means: The forecast that medium and large SaaS companies struggle as customers build what they want instead of renting an approximation, decided by inertia rather than by AI

concepts.label: Same bytes served
concepts.means: A refactoring proved by hashing what the live site serves before and after, not by reading the diff

concepts.label: Give the agent the screenshot
concepts.means: a synthetic user drives the browser from what is visible in a screenshot, never from the page's code, so confusion can be found

concepts.label: Scrolled is not read
concepts.means: Attended time on a section against its words is reading; a scroll past it is not.

concepts.label: Sealed files
concepts.means: An inner envelope inside any vault that seals chosen files to named people's public keys, with the private key held anywhere, including a service that logs and approves each decryption

concepts.label: Search as navigation
concepts.means: Type a word and walk into the graph around it, with suggestions that are all exact.

concepts.label: The second story
concepts.means: Why the system allowed the failure, beyond the first story of what happened; the third story is why the fix was not paid for.

concepts.label: Into the tool, not the chat
concepts.means: a secret travels from a one-time drop through a pipe into the tool that needs it, never into the prompt, transcript or model context

concepts.label: Sell, don't issue
concepts.means: A founder sells shares at a price rather than issuing them; the controllable founder keeps control.

concepts.label: Sell the maintenance
concepts.means: Vendors let users explore for free and sell them the work of keeping what they built working across releases

concepts.label: Sender-served structure
concepts.means: The message carries its actions, questions, decisions and status as blocks the recipient's agent can render with fidelity

concepts.label: The shared responsibility model for agents
concepts.means: A platform draws its line where it can see and touch, files, ports, the desktop, a tool call; above that line the business logic and the authority are the deployer's

concepts.label: Complexity and shipping
concepts.means: Knowing when to stop, keeping complexity down, and checks that prove a release is live.

concepts.label: Skill behaviour policy
concepts.means: A policy for one skill from three mandates, described, actual and granted, and the control that closes the gaps

concepts.label: Smaller models, more of them
concepts.means: Most work needs a model good enough for one job, language and culture, not a frontier model; agents should use the least agency that does the job

concepts.label: Software was the law
concepts.means: Business rules that screens enforced by omission stop being enforced once an agent calls the API the button called

concepts.label: An open-source sovereign cloud
concepts.means: A European cloud that is fully open source, compatible with the big clouds' APIs and federated across countries, regions and cities

concepts.label: A standard, not a server
concepts.means: A documented format with more than one implementation that agree, so where the objects live is a deployment choice and the server is the least interesting part

concepts.label: Startups and early access
concepts.means: Founding and launching: does anybody miss it, early access, go to market, investors.

concepts.label: The state of the thread
concepts.means: Ending a reply with a short state of the thread written for this reader, decided, open, next, on copy and sources, instead of the quoted wall

concepts.label: Story vaults and liquid content
concepts.means: The story kept as a graph of claims and evidence, with the article as one projection of it.

concepts.label: Strategy and positioning
concepts.means: Inertia, positioning and the SaaS shake-out.

concepts.label: Success breeds inertia
concepts.means: Wardley's climatic pattern: an installed base and past success make an incumbent slow to change, so new entrants initiate it

concepts.label: Supply chains
concepts.means: Chains of parties sharing data: food prices, software supply chains.

concepts.label: Survivorship bias
concepts.means: Studying only the winners makes practices unrelated to success look like its cause, because the failures are undersampled.

concepts.label: Synthetic users
concepts.means: Invented users and simulated runs that show what a design does before real people meet it.

concepts.label: The talk as a timeline
concepts.means: Slides, builds, animations and the demo written as beats that play on a clock while the speaker speaks to them; rehearsed, measured and changed like code

concepts.label: Taxonomy debt
concepts.means: Tags used once, ideas not shared between articles: the cost of classification left loose.

concepts.label: The big stick
concepts.means: The point at which a founder can credibly say I leave and you cannot replace me, and the contract hands power back.

concepts.label: The brief
concepts.means: A written commission for an agent or a person: what to build, for whom, with its limits.

concepts.label: The fork next door
concepts.means: Founders, customers and investors are each protected from the others because anyone can fork the code, and forks take hold only after a breakdown.

concepts.label: The four inputs of the voice
concepts.means: an agent sounds like its author through a corpus, a voice memo, a short list of wording rules and a reader who corrects

concepts.label: The immutable line
concepts.means: The level in a stack below which nothing changes, drawn as high as the evidence allows so that more of the system is fixed, exact and small

concepts.label: The keyring
concepts.means: A browser-only secrets store, one encrypted file per user, unlocked by a passkey with the PRF extension, that an administrator with full access cannot read.

concepts.label: The long tail
concepts.means: The users on old machines and old versions that projects drop because supporting them costs money nobody pays

concepts.label: The loop
concepts.means: A feature crossing editorial, product, engineering, sales and the founder closes in a day when every hand-off is a written brief and each part owns its own place and tests what it receives

concepts.label: The loop is the moat
concepts.means: the speed from a comment to an article to a shipped feature is what is hard to copy

concepts.label: The Mandate Stack
concepts.means: Many small agents, one written mandate each, everything connected as a graph, one human who sends; the eight-layer pattern RiskMandate runs on

concepts.label: Market and competitors
concepts.means: Who else sells it, at what price, and where the gap is.

concepts.label: Whether they miss it
concepts.means: the test of a product is whether anybody misses it when it is taken away, including the people who build it

concepts.label: This newsroom
concepts.means: The SGit Newsroom itself: its agent roles, its desks, its reader features, how it runs.

concepts.label: The reading list in a link
concepts.means: A curated list of articles carried in a link, by number, that opens the same list in a year.

concepts.label: The record
concepts.means: What was actually published, committed or logged, against which a claim is checked.

concepts.label: The site is an inbox
concepts.means: Every piece that arrives is undecided; deciding is the work, reading is one of the decisions, and the state to return to is empty

concepts.label: The monopoly, not the model
concepts.means: reporting was paid for by a local monopoly on distribution, the toll bridge, not by the advertising model; the web took the bridge

concepts.label: The tool loop
concepts.means: Hit a friction, build the tool as HTML in the same session, deploy it into the vault, use it, repeat; the vault as an app platform

concepts.label: The value of constraints
concepts.means: A design constraint removes both the possibility and the temptation of a bad decision, and the features come from solving the problems it creates

concepts.label: The industry wire
concepts.means: Industry news read live from a public-read vault that agents write to, one wire per subject.

concepts.label: Threat modelling
concepts.means: Naming the attacker before choosing the defence: threat models, attack trees, the security line.

concepts.label: One pipeline, three records
concepts.means: An agent's supply chain needs trusted inputs, a written mandate, and provable outputs and memory

concepts.label: A token budget
concepts.means: A hard limit per run on what model calls may spend, counted per provider, rather than a report after the fact

concepts.label: Trust as a service
concepts.means: a newsroom answers, on the record and with a warranty, whether it reported a claim and whether it still holds, sold per query

concepts.label: The two walls
concepts.means: An operating system separates by force only the kernel and the user account; inside one account there is no third wall between an agent and the user's credentials.

concepts.label: Undo is a list, not a promise
concepts.means: With the before and after of every change recorded, the inverse call can be written and the irreversible actions named

concepts.label: The vault
concepts.means: An encrypted, versioned store of files that a read key opens and a server cannot read.

concepts.label: Vault design
concepts.means: How a vault is built: append lanes, partial clones, files instead of a database.

concepts.label: Vault in vault
concepts.means: A link file in one vault points at another whose read key sits in an owner record, so an app's reads under the link are served from the child vault read-only

concepts.label: The vault of vaults
concepts.means: A private registry vault, run by an isolated agent session, whose only job is to hold the keys to the other vaults.

concepts.label: The voice memo
concepts.means: The owner's spoken memo, kept in the order he thought it, as the source of an article.

concepts.label: Wardley maps
concepts.means: Placing a thing on the evolution axis, from genesis to commodity, and arguing from where it sits.

concepts.label: What you measure is what you become
concepts.means: The metric an organisation rewards reshapes it; a metric is a hiring plan in disguise

concepts.label: The why card
concepts.means: A permission prompt that carries its reason, the change in reach, its cost, the path if declined and a record, and becomes a risk acceptance when the risk rises

concepts.label: Working in the open
concepts.means: Publishing the work a founder or newsroom usually does in private, drafts and decisions included, as part of the story
